clue.text: Like amateur in church, primarily

indicators.note: 'primarily' asks for each word's first, primary, letter

parts.note: first letters of Like, Amateur, In, Church

explanation.surface: A comment on the unpaid, untrained layperson helping out in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the letter source and the definition: laic means lay, belonging to the laity rather than the clergy, which is exactly how an amateur stands in church.
explanation.definitionFit: LAIC means lay, non-clerical, like the amateur as opposed to the professional clergy.

clue.text: Songwriters call up securing one in charts

indicators.note: the reversed call holds the I fast inside it

parts.note: charts, as in the top-forty lists

indicators.note: the whole group goes inside the word for charts

parts.note: to call out is to cry
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Songwriters phoning up to ask where their record sits in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call up' looks like one phrase meaning phone, but it splits in two: call is the word, and up, in a down clue, turns it over. The one goes inside that before the whole lot enters the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyricists write the words of songs.

clue.text: International sportsman with skill getting bronze — he enhanced many grounds

parts.note: a player picked for his country is a cap, or capped player
skill is ability
bronze is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A gifted international athlete winning a bronze medal, who also improves sports grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sportsman looking after pitches; the grounds are really the parks of English country houses. An international is called a cap because players once received a cap for each appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown was the 18th-century English landscape gardener who reshaped the grounds of many great estates.

clue.text: Bar bowler for match between close rivals

parts.note: your local is the nearby pub, a bar
a derby is the American name for a bowler hat

explanation.surface: Banning a bowler from a cricket match against the neighbouring team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' reads as a verb (ban) and 'bowler' as a cricketer; they are a pub and a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A local derby is a game between two teams from the same area, fierce because the rivals are close neighbours.

clue.text: Someone who's left something Eastern accepted by ambassador

parts.note: a legate is an envoy or ambassador, especially a papal one
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: An ambassador receiving an oriental item that someone bequeathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Someone who's left something' seems to describe a person who departed or made a will; it means the person something has been left to.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition turns on the passive sense of left: a legatee is the beneficiary a legacy was bequeathed to, not the person who died.

clue.text: Brief agreement raised as gesture of respect

parts.note: curt means brief, short

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the word makes it read from the bottom up

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A quick nod of assent given as a sign of deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' works only because this is a down clue: the word of agreement is written from the bottom upwards, after the word for brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsey is the bob with bent knees made as a mark of respect.

clue.text: Stolid politician, one accosted by drunk

indicators.note: the drunk closes in on both sides of the politician and the one

parts.note: a lush is a drunkard
Member of Parliament
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An unexcitable politician being buttonholed by a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accosted' suggests being harassed; here it means surrounded, with the drunk's letters falling on both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumpish means heavy and dull, as a stolid person is.

clue.text: One being taught abroad scanned huge text for translation

indicators.note: translating turns the letters into something new, rearranging them

parts.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A foreign pupil scanning a large document in order to translate it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits a language student so well that the anagram hides in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An exchange student is taught in a foreign country while a student from there comes the other way.

clue.text: Police HQ's measures

definitions.meaning: Scotland Yard, London police headquarters, plus the possessive 's
imperial units of length, three feet each

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Yard' is Scotland Yard, headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police; the Yard's becomes YARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Yards are units of length, just under a metre each.

clue.text: Someone going mad put butter on signalling device

parts.note: a butter here is something that butts, like a ram
a pager beeps to signal you

explanation.surface: A lunatic spreading butter on a beeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts, rhyming with putter; 'on' in an across clue places it first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampager is someone rushing about wildly, going on the rampage.

clue.text: Friend's stable occupation

definitions.meaning: British slang for a mate; the 's is 'is'

explanation.walkthrough: Mucker is British slang for a mate. A mucker is also one who mucks out stables, clearing the muck, so the job is the stable occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucker is informal British for a close friend, and also names the stable worker who shovels muck.

clue.text: Fight against doctor in Ulster, perhaps

indicators.note: the doctor goes inside the coat

parts.note: an ulster is a long heavy overcoat
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Taking on a doctor in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster looks like the Irish province but is the coat named after it, and 'perhaps' flags it as one example of a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to combat a disease or a rival is to fight against it.

clue.text: Jump over insects in tight trousers

parts.note: to skip is to jump lightly
ants are insects

explanation.surface: Leaping over bugs while squeezed into tight trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay splits one letter later than the answer does, so the P of the jump becomes the start of the trousers. 'Over' puts the jump first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are close-fitting stretchy trousers, originally worn for skiing.

clue.text: Fix match

definitions.meaning: a knockout game, as in a cup fixture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix match' reads as match-rigging; it is two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie is to fix or fasten; a tie is also a match, as in a cup tie.

clue.text: Place for hard work where someone having a row's unknown

parts.note: a sculler rows a boat
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A workplace where the person in a quarrel is a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having a row' suggests an argument (rhymes with cow), but it is rowing a boat; the 's is 'has', attaching the unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: The scullery was the back room for rough kitchen work like washing pots.

clue.text: Expression of disgust that man's picked up as Poet Laureate once

parts.note: that man is = he's
ugh expresses disgust

explanation.surface: Someone's revolted cry being overheard and turned into a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests hearing a sound, but here it means lifted and held: HE'S holds UGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Ted Hughes held the post of British Poet Laureate from 1984 until his death in 1998, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Angus turned up with mysterious source of sweetness

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning the name upwards reverses it

parts.note: Gus is a short form of Angus
arcane means mysterious

explanation.surface: A man called Angus showing up with a secret supply of sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the pet form of the name is used: Angus is shortened to Gus before being reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar cane is the tall grass from which much of the world's sugar is extracted.

clue.text: Not moving? It's shocking

definitions.meaning: the charge built up on a jumper or door handle that zaps you

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's shocking' sounds like outrage, but it describes static electricity, which gives small shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means stationary; static, the electricity, is what zaps you off a door handle.

clue.text: Anything from Yorkshire upset a couple

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting the word tips it upside down

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect, especially Yorkshire, for anything

explanation.surface: Two Yorkshire folk annoyed by just about anything.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire speech owt means anything and nowt means nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a couple of things is a pair of them, and here 'a couple' stands for the number.

clue.text: Ascending selection from Pat's electric keyboard instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means reading from the bottom up
the answer is a run of letters selected from inside the words that follow

parts.note: seven letters running from inside Pat's across the start of electric

explanation.surface: Choosing from someone's electric keyboard, playing a rising scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electric keyboard' looks like a single phrase for the definition; the electric belongs to the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a small keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal bars, heard in the Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy.

clue.text: Fashion designers (not one English) supplying outfit

indicators.note: to fashion the letters is to shape them into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
E for English, one of them removed

explanation.surface: A fashion house, short of one English designer, providing a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion designers' reads as one phrase, but fashion is the instruction to rearrange. Only one of the two Es in DESIGNERS goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense: to dress a person, or an actor for a show, is to provide their clothes.

clue.text: Comical stand-up, collector of dirty material

indicators.note: a comical arrangement of the letters is a silly jumble of them

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A stand-up comic who collects blue, smutty material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty material' suggests a comedian's filthy jokes; it is literal dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan collects the dirt swept up from the floor.

clue.text: Talk at length about old stamp

parts.note: ex means former, old
to stamp is to pound

explanation.surface: Going on and on about a vintage postage stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old stamp' paints a stamp collector; stamp is a verb, pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound on something is to explain it in detail, at length.

clue.text: Draws little man as going after fling, being retired

indicators.note: the AS is placed after the reversed fling

parts.note: Tom, the short form of Thomas, is a man's name made little

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the fling runs backwards

parts.note: to lob is to fling
taken as written

explanation.surface: A retired man sketching a small figure after a brief affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws' looks like a verb for sketching and 'fling' like a romance; they are raffles and a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle-style lottery, a prize draw.

clue.text: Carry on miles — something regarded with awe

parts.note: to tote is to carry
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: Pressing on for miles with something sacred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry on' reads as one phrase meaning continue; it is carry (TOTE) with M placed on after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a sacred emblem or revered object, treated with awe.

clue.text: One who is hard up's written article about uranium

indicators.note: the article goes around, about, the uranium

parts.note: a paper is a written article
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A broke writer producing a piece on uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a, an or the; here it is a whole written piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauper is a very poor person, someone hard up.

clue.text: Lark about entertaining old soldiers

indicators.note: turning about sends the word back the other way
the reversed word hosts the old, holding it inside

parts.note: a lark is fun, sport
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Messing about while putting on a show for veteran servicemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old soldiers' reads as veterans; old gives only O, and soldiers is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain plural synonym: troops are soldiers in general, as in 'sending in the troops'.

clue.text: Scales, perhaps, everything back after cut

parts.note: to prune is to cut back

indicators.note: 'back' says everything is written backwards

parts.note: all is everything

explanation.surface: Weighing scales, or fish scales, all turned over after trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: Scales looks like weighing equipment; it is the surname of the British actress Prunella Scales, best known as Sybil in Fawlty Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella is the first name of Prunella Scales, so 'Scales, perhaps' is one Prunella.

clue.text: Observed in animated dances

indicators.note: the letters dance about into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone watched at a lively dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observed' pretends to mean seen; here it is observed as a custom is kept up. The 'in' belongs to the letters, not the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe a rule or tradition is to maintain it.

clue.text: Book dedication of egotist

parts.note: a book's dedication begins 'To ...'
an egotist always thinks of me

explanation.surface: The self-regarding author who dedicates his book to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: An egotist's dedication would read 'To me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym with a shade: the word is used for a book that is heavy, weighty or scholarly.
